title: Effect of WC Addition on the Hardness of Ti-Zr Alloy
content: Ti-Zr alloys have displayed commendable mechanical and corrosion resistance attributes, largely due to the zirconium content. The remarkable biocompatibility and corrosion resistance of titanium alloys are attributed to the formation of a stable, dense oxide layer, predominantly TiO2 [1]. Introducing additional elements to the Ti-Zr base can modify its properties. Specifically, appropriate zirconium quantities enhance super elasticity recovery and bolster the emergence of shape memory traits. Ti-Zr alloys have demonstrated good mechanical strength and corrosion resistance due to the presence of Zr. However, to achieve the necessary hardness in Ti-Zr alloys, it is essential to subject them to heat treatment. Therefore, the use of WC is a viable option to enhance hardness without the application of heat treatments. The addition of WC to a Ti-Zr alloy offers multiple advantages. Firstly, WC increases the hardness and wear resistance of the alloy. Since WC has very high hardness, adding particles enhances the overall hardness of the Ti-Zr alloy, making it more resistant to wear. This study aims to assess the microstructure and mechanical attributes of Ti-Zr alloys with varied WC percentages (5, 10, and 15%). These alloys, synthesized via electric arc melting, were examined using optical microscopy, microhardness tests, and XRD; to observe the enhanced in mechanical properties and microstructure.
